doagh-famine-village: An open-air museum on the Inishowen Peninsula telling the story of a Donegal family from the Great Famine to the present day.
the-model: Sligo's art gallery and home of the Niland Collection, with important works by Jack B. Yeats and free admission to the galleries.
joyce-tower-museum: An 1804 Martello tower where Ulysses opens, today a free museum with a Joycean collection and views over Dublin Bay.
derrigimlagh: A Connemara bogland with two 20th-century landmarks: the ruins of Marconi's transatlantic radio station and the memorial to Alcock and Brown's crossing.
forty-foot: A historic sea-bathing spot at Sandycove, at the southern tip of Dublin Bay, with a year-round swimming tradition.
chester-beatty: A museum of world cultures inside Dublin Castle, with free entry and collections from Asia, the Middle East, North Africa and Europe.
king-johns-castle-carlingford: A 12th-century Norman fortress above Carlingford Lough, with a medieval hall and views of the Mourne Mountains.
mount-leinster-nine-stones: The highest point of the Blackstairs Mountains (795 m), with the Nine Stones lookout and views over four counties.
oak-park-forest-park: Woodland of oak and beech with trails, lakes and Oak Park Lake, near the town of Carlow.
borris-house: The ancestral home of the MacMurrough Kavanaghs, kings of Leinster, with Tudor halls and a craft market.
huntington-castle-gardens: A 1625 castle of the Durdin-Robertson family, with medieval cellars, walled gardens and a druidic temple.
ducketts-grove: Victorian Gothic ruins of the Duckett mansion, with restored walled gardens and a public park.
altamont-gardens: Romantic 18th-century gardens with a lake, arboretum and the "azalea walk" — free entry.
brownshill-dolmen: A dolmen with the largest capstone in Europe: 100 tonnes of granite resting on 5,000-year-old support stones.
millmount-fort-museum: A fortress on a Norman motte with views over Drogheda, housing the county museum and the Martello tower.
carlingford-lough-greenway: A 10 km greenway along the lough, between Carlingford and Newry, with views of the Mourne Mountains.
mellifont-abbey: Ireland's first Cistercian abbey (1142), with a unique octagonal lavabo and evocative ruins.
monasterboice: A monastic site with Ireland's most famous high crosses, including the 10th-century Muiredach's Cross.
proleek-dolmen: A megalithic dolmen with a 40-tonne capstone, wrapped in legend — whoever lands a stone on top will have good luck.
carlingford: A preserved medieval village on the shores of Carlingford Lough, with town walls, a castle and the Carlingford Oyster Festival.
mondello-park: Ireland's only international racing circuit, with race meetings open to the public and driving experiences.
lullymore-heritage-park: A discovery park on a limestone island in the boglands, with a train ride, playground, mini golf and peatland history.
donadea-forest-park: A forest park with trails, a lake, the Aylmer castle tower and the 9/11 Memorial Garden.
maynooth-castle: A Fitzgerald stronghold of the powerful Earls of Kildare, on the campus of Ireland's oldest university.
pollardstown-fen: Ireland's largest fen (alkaline marsh), a nature reserve with boardwalks and rare plants of glacial origin.
